title: Point the visual capture tools at the proven hardware-GPU transport, and capture the twelve motion sequences that had never been captured at all
state: complete — the full Deck and 11 of 12 motion sequences captured on an RTX A5000, evidence class read from the renderer string, self-test green and mutation-proven
overlap_declared: tools/visual/deck.mjs is claimed by W1-30V, who is live (checked with tools/ownership.mjs --for). My edit is confined to four places: the import block; the launch call; the renderer probe, which moves VERBATIM into tools/visual/lib/renderer-class.mjs and keeps its comment; and the manifest's evidence-class fields, which keep every name they had and gain three. One further change is a bug fix rather than a feature: call() reached the harness through browser.mjs's h(), which routes a page-side throw into die() -> process.exit, so a try/catch around it could not catch anything and one bad setup ended the sweep with no manifest at all. deck.mjs's own goTo() carries a comment about exactly that failure, worked around case by case; call() now speaks to the page directly and returns the error as a value. tools/runpod/lib/http-transport.mjs belongs to gpu-transport-20260814, whose status reads done; the change is one retry wrapper around upload(), and its 20-arm self-test still passes. tools/harness/vt-*.mjs are claimed by nobody live.

what_changed.headline: The Deck, the motion runner and the four vt-* tools can all run on a real GPU now. `node tools/visual/gpu-deck.mjs --profile full` sends one batched job to a Pod and brings back one tar.
what_changed.measured: 288 stills, 0 red, 143 s; 11 of 12 motion sequences, 2,220 frames, 318 s; total 10.02 min, $0.045, on RTX A5000 y7kvxe5sggeqhj. Renderer reported by the browser: ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.312 (NVIDIA NVIDIA RTX A5000 (0x00002231)), NVIDIA).
what_changed.default: local SwiftShader. Hardware is --gpu hardware, and only gpu-deck.mjs ever rents anything.

what_changed.headline: The twelve motion sequences the Deck has declared since it was generated are captured for the first time.
what_changed.measured: walk, run, sprint-stop, turn-180, roll-4dir, jump-land, attack-light, attack-heavy, block-hit, boundary-walk, day-night all green with every frame distinct; spell RED with the reason (setCatalyst wants a catalyst KIND: rod, not an item id). Contact sheets at every 6th frame are committed under reports/visual-truth/deck-motion/hw-full/contact/.
what_changed.checks: a sequence goes red if the picture did not change (frame hashes), if the PLAYER did not change (position, body yaw, camera yaw, anim, state), if a cast fired no magic event, or if any setup step was refused.

what_changed.headline: evidence_class is now decided by the renderer string the browser reported, never by which path was requested, in one shared module every capture tool routes through.
what_changed.self_test: node tools/visual/gpu-deck.mjs --self-test — 10 arms green. The two arms that matter do not fabricate the disputed input: the software arm reads the string off a live local browser, the hardware arm reads it out of docs/shots/2026-08-14-gpu-transport/gpu-smoke.json, written by an RTX A5000 on a live Pod. A third arm requires the two to DIFFER, which is the HAZARDS §0 fifth-failure-shape guard.
what_changed.mutation: node tools/visual/test/mutate-renderer-class.mjs — M1 (fail open again) reddens 1 arm, M2 (let the request decide) reddens 4 including the red control, and the file is restored byte-identically.

defects_found_in_the_tools_being_joined: browser.mjs's h() turns a page-side throw into process.exit, so both the Deck and the motion runner had a try/catch that could not catch. spawn() threw and the first local motion run died at sequence 9 of 12 with NO manifest — the exact failure the Deck's header promises it will not produce. Both now call the page directly.

pop-0027-infantry is a population row, not a combat archetype; the engine refuses it by name. tools/harness/vt-play.mjs has been asking for it, so its fight section has been failing into a catch. inf_trash is a real one.

PodAgentClient.upload had no retry: a 20 MiB snapshot died at 16 MiB with a bodyless HTTP 404 from the RunPod proxy and ended a paid run before a frame was captured. It now retries the WHOLE upload three times (a chunk retry could duplicate bytes into the middle of a tarball; restarting at byte 0 is idempotent).

pod_hygiene.all_terminated: each by its own run's mandatory cleanup, with deletion API-confirmed
pod_hygiene.final_check: node tools/runpod/cli.mjs cleanup --dry-run — nothing of mine; two live Pods belonging to other agents listed as PROTECTED and left alone

hazards_hit: tools/contention.mjs said WAIT (load 13-25 over 4 cores) for most of the session. I proceeded, one browser at a time, and say so here as the tool asks. Local timings from this session are not comparable with anything.

Disk went from 12 GB free to 2.6 GB free during the piece. The full run's tar is 184 MB and --return sheets exists precisely to bound it; two raw-frame directories were added to .gitignore so a routine `git add -A` cannot sweep a quarter-gigabyte of PNGs into the tree (HAZARDS §3).
The first full run was lost to the un-retried upload above, at a cost of $0.007 and four minutes.
next_step: A fresh-context critic. The four things most worth attacking: (1) run `--catalyst rod` and settle the one red sequence; (2) run frame-stats.mjs across the 288 hardware stills — street-lilmoth already flags occluded,no-detail,flat-tone and nobody has looked at the other 287 on hardware; (3) add the 144-frame orbit to remoteCommand() so the character gate runs natively too; (4) attack the SwiftShader-versus-hardware comparison — it is six shots at one time of day, and W1-30-EVIDENCE §4's falsifier asks specifically whether the two renderers ever disagree on a DELTA.
